name: MADNESS
listed_description: Multiresolution Adaptive Numerical Environment for Scientific Simulation.
reason: No numeric comparison against any named baseline found. The README (GPL-2.0, 221 stars) describes capabilities, conda packages and downstream projects (TiledArray, MPQC, Tequila, FrayedEnds) and has no benchmark section; the pymadness README path 404s. A search for MADNESS timings against NWChem or Gaussian-basis codes found only accuracy discussions (multiwavelet vs Gaussian basis accuracy), not speed. The SISC 2016 paper (arXiv 1507.01888) and the readthedocs and doxygen sites are on blocked hosts, so any comparison inside them could not be checked.

name: Minerva
listed_description: A fast and flexible system for deep learning.
reason: No numeric comparison against a named baseline. The README (Apache-2.0, 712 stars, archived 2019-10-15) gives training speed in images per second on 4 GTX Titan cards (AlexNet 189.63 on 1 card, 632.09 on 4; VGGNet 14.37 and 50.26; GoogLeNet 82.47 and 309.27) but those are self-scaling numbers with no Caffe or other framework row. The only Caffe comparison is a training-error-versus-time image (hosted on cloud.githubusercontent.com, blocked) with no numbers in the text; the wiki pages opened contain no benchmarks. The NIPS 2014 workshop paper on web.stanford.edu is blocked.

name: MPQC
listed_description: The Massively Parallel Quantum Chemistry program, MPQC, computes properties of atoms and molecules from first principles using the time independent Schrodinger equation.
reason: No numeric comparison against Psi4, NWChem, Gaussian or Q-Chem found. The README (GPL-3.0-or-later, 81 stars) shows only strong scaling of one CCSD iteration for a uracil trimer in 6-31G* (1290 s on one 16-core node of the BlueRidge cluster, speedup plot as an image), which is self-scaling with no competing program. The repo wiki has no comparison, and the cited J. Chem. Theory Comput. and J. Phys. Chem. A papers are on blocked hosts; a search found no direct MPQC4 versus NWChem or Psi4 timing.

name: ncnn
listed_description: A high-performance neural network inference computing framework optimized for mobile platforms.
reason: Directional claim only. Older READMEs (2018 to 2020 tags) say ncnn 'runs faster than all known open source frameworks on mobile phone cpu' with no numbers; the current README says only 'high-performance'. benchmark/README.md lists ncnn-only millisecond timings for about 100 devices with no other framework as a baseline (int8 and fp32 are both ncnn). Third-party multi-framework benchmarks exist (MDLBench paper arXiv 2202.06512 and its repo UbiquitousLearning/MobileDLFrameworksBenchmark, whose CPUResult folder holds only .gitkeep; embedded-ai.bench, archived with a licence barring republication of results; XiaoMi mobile-ai-bench with no result tables in its README) but no ncnn-versus-baseline number could be opened because arxiv.org and the paper hosts are blocked; the mmdeploy benchmark has no same-hardware ncnn versus PyTorch or ONNX Runtime latency.
